full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque, J. : These two rules were issued on 18.1.82 at the instance of the plaintiff petitioner Bangla Jalpari Lines (Pvt) Ltd. against the judgment. and order dated 27.11.81 passed by Mr. MA Rashid Subordinate Judge, 3rd  Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case Nos. 59 and 60 of 1981 arising out of Money Suit No. 152 of 1981. At the time of issuance of the Rule it was directed to hear both the Rules analogously. The trial Court also passed one judgment on hearing the Miscellaneous Case Nos. 59 and 60 of 1981 on 27.11.81 analogously. 

 2. Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1981 was filed by defendant petitioner OP No. 1 the Continental Grain Co (Canada) Ltd. represented by their local agent Maritime Enterprises, Chittagong who claimed to be the Charterer of, the vessel in question, namely, MV Regent Ranger. Miscellaneous case No. 60 of 1981 was filed by petitioner OP No. 1 M/s Sanko Steamship Co. Ltd. Tokyo represented by their local agent Pragoti Shipping Bangladesh Ltd., Chittagong, who claimed to be the owner of the said vessel MV Regent Ranger. Both the cases were under Order 38, rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure for releasing the bank guarantee furnished in the ease for releasing the said vessel from the order of conditional attachment passed by the Court on 6.7.81 in Money Suit No. 152 of 1981. 

 3. The plaintiff petitioner filed Money Suit No. 152 of 1981 claiming recovery of a sum of Tk. 9,82,136.80 against the defendant No. 1 M/s Continental Grain Co. Ltd. (USA) and other 3 defendants, alleging them to be agent of the said defendant No. 1. After filing the said suit the plaintiff petitioner filed an application under Order 38, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure for attachment before judgment of the said vessel MV Regent Ranger alleging that the same belonged to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of whom defendant Nos. 3 and 4 are local agents and that. if the said.ship.left the:country after discharging the cargo., the plaintiff petitioner will not be able to execute the decree and the decree eventually passed will be frustrated. After hearing the plaintiff-petitioner the Court below on 6.7.81 passed the conditional order of attachment of the vessel. Thereafter the opposite party No. 1 the Continental Grain Co (Canada) Ltd. of Civil Revision No. 111 of 1981 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1981 on 14.7.81 and the opposite party No. 1 of M/s. Sanko Steamship Co. Ltd. Tokyo of Civil. Revision No. 112 of 1981 filed Miscellaneous case No. 60 of1981 under Order 38 rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the aforesaid order of attachment of the ship in question. After filing the said Miscellaneous Cases the petitioner of the respective Miscellaneous Case submitted a bank guarantee for the claimed amount in the suit and the Court below accepted the same by order dated 16.7.81 and released the ship MV Regent Ranger from attachment. 

 4. The case of the objector petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1981 was that the ship MV Regent Ranger originally belonged to Regent Orchid Shipping Inc. of Monrovia, Liberia and the said company demised the said vessel to M/s Sanko Steamship Co. Ltd., Tokyo, Japan and the said company as the disponent owner of the said vessel entered into an voyage charter agreement with the objector-petitioner (opposite party No. 1 in CR No. 111 of 1982) M/s Continental Grain Co. (Canada) Ltd. on 14.7.81 for one voyage from Vancouver to Chittagong for carrying oil-seeds. In terms of the said charter party and according to the established shipping practice the objector-petitioner as voyage charterer is obliged to release the vessel on completion of her contracted voyage whereupon the vessel was reverted to the actual possession of the owner. It was further contented that the ingredients of the Order 38, rule 5 of the Code of Civil -Procedure were absent in plaintiff petitioner's application for attachment before judgment as there was no attempt to remove the said vessel from the jurisdiction of Court with intent to obstruct or delay the execution of any decree that might be passed. 

 5. The objector-petitioner (opposite party No. 1 in CR No. 112 of 1982) in Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1981 claimed to be the disponent owner of the ship MV Regent Ranger on the basis of charter by demise from the original registered owner M/s Regent Orchard Shipping Inc. of Monrovia, Liberia. Under voyage charter party agreement dated 27.4.81 with M/s Shanko Steamship Co Ltd. (Petitioner in Miscellaneous Case No. 60 of 1981) the said vessel was chartered by M/s Continental Grain Co. (Canada) Ltd. (Petitioner in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1981) for one voyage from Vancouver to Chittagong/Chalna for carrying oil seeds paying therefore freight to the said objector petitioner. In terms of voyage charter party the said vessel was to revert to the objector-petitioner on completion of the voyage on discharge of the cargo. It was further contented that the plaintiff petitioner with a malafide motive concealed the existence of the voyage charter-party and falsely stated in their petition for attachment before judgment that the vessel belonged to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of Money Suit No. 152 of 1981 and that as the vessel did not belong to the defendants it could not be attached. 

 6. The plaintiff opposite party (petitioner herein) contested both the cases by filing two separate written objections denying all the material allegations and asserting that the Ship MV Regent Ranger was under the ownership and full control of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on the basis of time charter. That the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are the owners of Continental Grain Co. (Canada) Ltd. and that since the vessel in question was under the control of defendant Nos. I and 2 on the basis of time charter the ownership of the vessel for the purpose of attachment was with the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and not with the alleged owner of the vessel, who had no control over the ship MV Regent Ranger at the time of attachment of the ship. 

 7. Both the parties examined only one witness each in support of their respective case and filed documents which were marked exhibits. After considering the oral as well as the documentary evidence the Court below came to the following conclusions : 

 "So the charter party in question that stands in the name of M/s Continental Grain Co. (Canada) Ltd. can not be regarded as charter party between defendant No. 1 M/s Continental Grain Company USA and M/s Sanko Steamship Co. Tokyo, Japan. So for liability of defendant No. 1 the claimant Sanko Steamship Co. cannot be held responsible. Again the charter-party is of a voyage charter. In case of a voyage charter-party the ownership and control or for that matter the possession, of the vessel remains with the owner and not with the Charterer. For that reason also the plaintiff can not attach the vessel. It is settled law that a property to be attached before judgment must be the property of defendants. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff OP has referred to the decision laid down in PLD 1964 (SC) 222 and has argued that the inquiry that effects the decision in a claim case is the inquiry of ascertainment of possession. For reasons detailed above the decision quoted by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff OP does not apply to the case before this Court. In any case defendants are not even the temporary owner of the vessel even if it is conceded that they are charterer for the simple reason that the charter is a voyage charter only." 

 8. Mr. Mustafa Niak Muhammad, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in both the cases submitted that the Court below failed to notice and consider that the petitioner in Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1981 i.e. M/s Continental Grain Company (Canada) Ltd. is a sister concern of the defendant No. 1 in Money Suit No. 152 of 1981 i.e. M/s Continental Grain Co. (USA) Ltd. and the share-holders and directors of both the companies are the same as will appear from the address of the M/s Continental Grain Co. (Canada) Ltd. given in the contract between the Government of Bangladesh and M/s Continental Grain Co. (USA) Ltd. He submitted that the petitioner in the respective Miscellaneous Case has concealed the time charter agreement and has produced a voyage charter agreement to suppress the fact of time charter. He further submitted that under the time charter possession of the ship in question is made ever to the charterer for the period of the charter and during that period the ship could be kept under attachment as owner has no right or possession of the ship during the period of time charter. 

 9. Mr. Nurul Islam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party in both the cases submitted that in the absence of production of time charter by the plaintiff petitioner it cannot be said on the basis of mere assertion of the petitioner that the ship in question was hired under the time charter and the learned Court below rightly held after considering the charter party agreement that it was a voyage charter. He further submitted that in the voyage charter the ownership and possession remain with the owner and the charterer acquires neither any right of ownership nor any right of possession over the ship. As soon as the voyage ends and the cargoes arc discharged the charter ends and the ship reverts to the owner and as such no question of attachment of the ship after discharging of the cargo arises. 

 The essence of the modern form of time charter, on the other hand, is that under it the ship-owner agrees with the time charterer that during a certain named period he will render services by his master and crew to carry the goods which are put on board his ship by or on behalf of the time charterer. In this case, notwithstanding the temporary right of the charterer to have his goods loaded and conveyed in the vessel, the ownership and also the possession of the ship remain in the original owner through the master and crew, who continue to be his servants. The ship owner's remuneration is usually termed "hire" and is generally calculated at a monthly rate on the tonnage of the ship. 

 12. From the aforesaid authoritative description it is clear that even if the contention of the petitioner is accepted and it is found that the ship in question reached territorial waters of Bangladesh under a time charter the ownership and also the possession of the ship remained in the original owner through the master and the crew who continued to be his servants. The opposite party No. 1 in Civil Revision No. 111 of 1982 being a voyage charterer as found by the Court below and the defendant No. 1 not being the owner of the ship in any manner the ship in question was not liable to be attached before judgment at the instance of the petitioner. It appears that the court below by the impugned judgment and order dated 27.11.81 allowed both the Miscellaneous cases and directed to release the Bank Guarantee furnished by the objector petitioner (opposite party in the respective case). Thereafter by letter dated 17.12.81 the Bank concerned was intimated about the aforesaid order and requested to cancel the Bank guarantee. On receipt of the said letter the Bank in question cancelled the Bank guarantee. It appears that this Court passed an order of stay on 18.1.82 of the operation of the impugned, judgment and order dated 27.11.81. It also appears that the Bank Guarantee in question was cancelled before this order of stay was passed on 18.1.82 and communicated. It further appears that the ship in Question left the jurisdiction of the Court after furnishing the aforesaid Bank Guarantee accepted by the Court below on 16.7.81. It further appears that by order dated 10.7.82 the Court below directed to extend the Bank Guarantee up to 10.11.82 over-looking the fact that the Bank Guarantee was cancelled before the order of stay passed by this Court on 18.1.82. It further appears that on 23.9.82 an application was filed for vacating the order dated 10.7.82 for extending the period of Bank Guarantee stating the above fact of cancellation of the bank guarantee as a result of the impugned order before the order of stay was passed by this Court on 18.1.82. It further appears from the order dated 6.5.83 that the Court below directed for extending Bank Guarantee up to 30.6.82. It further appears that no Bank Guarantee was extended as the Bank Guarantee in question was already cancelled after the impugned order and before order of stay.
